result:
G4 now refuses a submission when an in-scope initiative has a dependency whose schedule is Unknown and nobody has recorded a mitigation. Every required check exited 0, and there are no migrations, new endpoints or contract changes. The DG2 validator (`--historical`) passed both at the start and at the end.

**What changed**
- **Rule:** `g4.roadmap` now lists `g4.schedule_unknown` with the text `'Schedule unknown: {dependency code}'` and pointer `/dependencies/{id}`. It applies to an unresolved dependency into an in-scope initiative that carries the `schedule.unknown` flag and has a blank mitigation. Recording a mitigation or filling in the missing dates clears it.
- **Where:** `workflows/g4.ts` has the new rule. `portfolio/gate-facts.ts` supplies the flag by reusing the existing `schedule.ts` flags rather than re-implementing them.
- **If the facts aren't loaded:** G4 stays incomplete with "Roadmap" rather than treating it as no conflict.
- **Both flags at once:** a dependency with both a late predecessor and a missing date is listed under both codes, and one mitigation clears both. I recorded this choice in ADR-0021 §11 item 3.
- **Tests:**
  - A unit test checks the item text and that G4 stays incomplete when the facts aren't loaded.
  - An integration test refuses the submission and lists both `Schedule unknown: DEP-nn` items. A mitigation clears one item and setting the needed-by date clears the other.
  - Every existing G4 test is unchanged and still passes. The end-to-end test creates no dependencies, so it didn't need changing.
- **Web:** I added the `g4__schedule_unknown` labels to the English and Arabic `gates.json` files (Arabic is provisional). The G4 view looks labels up from the code generically, so nothing else on the web side changed.
- **Docs:**
  - ADR-0021 §7 and §11 item 3 now state the new item.
  - ADR-0023 §1 now matches the wave model as built: the source text is the label, there are no label overrides, and no columns were added.
  - `p3-work-split.md` §9 has a new item 22.

**Checks**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm -r typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm -r build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm lint` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm openapi:lint` | exit 0 |
| prettier check (all tracked and untracked files) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm test`, locale unset | exit 0, 1523 tests passed |
| `pnpm test`, `C.UTF-8` | exit 0, 1523 tests passed |
| `pnpm test:integration` (PostgreSQL 16.13 on port 23450) | exit 0, 55 files, 788 tests passed |

**Failures during development, all fixed and re-run green**
- The first typecheck exited 2 because my new unit test set an optional field to `undefined`. The test now leaves the field out.
- The first targeted G4 integration run exited 1. The shared fixture can't create two selected initiatives in one world, so I made the predecessor a draft initiative with planned dates. I didn't edit the shared fixture.

**Open points**
- D-079 is cited in the code and ADRs, but it isn't in `decisions.md` yet, as the assignment says it is added at the freeze.
- Untracked top-level entries such as `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, `.mcp.json` and `CLAUDE.local.md` come from the sandbox, not from this work. Leave them out of the commit.
- If another wave-6 task also adds a §9 amendment to `p3-work-split.md`, the two may conflict, and item 22 may need renumbering.

The handback is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG3/T-DG3-BE-F-backend-workflow-engineer.md`, and the logs with exit codes are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG3/T-DG3-BE-F-evidence/`. Nothing is committed yet, ready for you to merge.
